gen-dafont-disorder-gf-noto-sans-bugines: Noto Sans Buginese reads modern and open, with letter mouths left like unjoined chalk arcs. Disorder up top is raw and set wide apart, its curves flat of any stress, so a long run of the plain sans below feels quietly composed by comparison.
gen-dafont-disorder-gf-noto-sans-carian: Loose, raw and a bit rowdy up top. Noto Sans Carian takes over below with terminals held apart like open scissor blades, while Disorder keeps its stroke edges running parallel through every curve.
gen-dafont-disorder-gf-noto-sans-chakma: Disorder has no swelling where curves meet stems, which gives it a raw edge. Noto Sans Chakma sits beneath with lowercase packed up toward the caps and open mouths on the s, so the two feel like shouting and then explaining.
gen-dafont-disorder-gf-noto-sans-cham: Noto Sans Cham reads modern and clean, its tall rounded lowercase leaving generous entry space into every c. And Disorder, with its unvarying line thickness, would hold a long stretch of that text against a raw, chaotic headline.
gen-dafont-disorder-gf-noto-sans-cheroke: Disorder is chaotic and raw, built from tubular, wire-like letterforms. Noto Sans Cherokee follows in a tall band of letters with short stalks above and an e left wide open at the terminal, giving the page a steadier footing.
gen-dafont-disorder-gf-noto-sans-chorasm: Noto Sans Chorasmian has curves that stop short instead of closing in, with a large x-height and short ascenders. Noto Sans Chorasmian is the quiet half here; Disorder, drawn like bent copper pipe, earns its keep big and brief.
gen-dafont-disorder-gf-noto-sans-coptic: Noto Sans Coptic reads clean and contemporary, with a texture where the middle zone dominates each line and open mouths on s and c. Disorder's true monoline drawing keeps the headline raw, while the body settles down.
gen-dafont-disorder-gf-noto-sans-cuneifo: Disorder is chaotic and raw, free of hairlines and swells, with glyphs set well apart. And Noto Sans Cuneiform stays clean beneath it, its e opening up and its lowercase swollen like inflated glass beads over a whole page.
gen-dafont-disorder-gf-noto-sans-deseret: Noto Sans Deseret reads approachable, with open apertures that aid legibility. Its high, wide-looking lowercase and squat ascenders keep a long passage easygoing, while Disorder's curves match its stems exactly and stay loud.
gen-dafont-disorder-gf-noto-sans-devanag: Noto Sans Devanagari reads neutral and modern, with an open lower curve on the g and capitals that blend into lowercase. Noto Sans Devanagari is the compact skyline against Disorder's raw, single-thickness outlines, and that gap is the whole appeal.
